evidence_units.text: White believes peace is not a mood. It is a structure: rules that hold, shelter that lasts, and obligations people can trust under pressure.
Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

One way to explore White is a Commander deck that builds protection into the table state: widen the board, defend the key piece, and let structure turn survival into pressure. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
Explore Protective Tokens, Taxes and Rules, Equipment and Guardians. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
Choose whether protection serves a wide board, a taxed table, or one equipped guardian, then keep enough interaction to preserve that plan.
Protect the engine, keep the standards clear, and do not spend your last shield before the table commits its real threat.
This may fit if you value shared standards, protection of the vulnerable, dependable obligations, and group safety over private exception.
Watch for this tension: White challenges Black's self-priority and Red's unrestrained immediacy, while Green can question whether White's systems listen to living reality.
